 Hon'Ble Sri Justice J. Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No.23704 of 2017
Order:

entities.text: Shahzad Begum, vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a Writ, Order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus by declaring the inaction of the respondent authorities in acting on the representations submitted by the petitioner particularly the representation dated 04.07.2017 as illegal, arbitrary and violative of principles of natural justice and consequently direct the respondents authorities to act on the representation submitted by the petitioner dated 04.07.2017 and allot the left out land in Sy. No.
331/1, on the Gajwel to Sangapur Road, which is in adjacent to the plot hold by the petitioner in Sy No. 331/1 by way of land to land compensation by proper valuation of the same and to pass ..."

2. Heard Sri Syed Minaaz, learned counsel, representing Sri M.Saleem, learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition, appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.2 to 4.
No representation on behalf of respondent Nos.1 and 5.
With the consent of respective parties, the writ petition is disposed of at the stage of admission.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is owner and possessor of the land to an extent of 266.38 square yards in MIG plot No.7 situated in Sy.Nos.334, 337, 338 and 331 of Gajwel Town.
The Government had taken the said land for the purpose of construction of Integrated Official Complex in Gajwel Town.
The petitioner has submitted representation on 04.07.2017 before respondent No.2 requesting him to allot other plot covered by Sy.No.331/1.
In spite of repeated requests made by the petitioner, respondent authorities have not taken any steps to consider the same.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader submits that if the representation submitted by the petitioner dated 04.07.2017 is still pending, respondent No.2 will consider the same in accordance with law and requested this Court to grant reasonable time and the same was not disputed by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

5. Taking into consideration of the submissions made by the respective parties, without expressing any view on merits of the case, respondent No.2 is directed to consider the representation submitted by the petitioner dated 04.07.2017 and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, within a period of two (2) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, if not already disposed of.
